Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Real feature request from the owner about the mod detail page's "Recommended Server" panel.

## Current state (from a real screenshot the owner shared)
The mod detail page (`app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx` and the portal equivalent `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`) has a plain-text panel: "RECOMMENDED SERVER — Works well on Minecraft — 2 GB / 10 slots (2 GB RAM) or higher — deploy one." with "deploy one" as a plain inline text link. Find this exact panel (search for "RECOMMENDED SERVER" or "Works well on" or the `RecommendedPlan` type in `lib/mods-catalog.ts` — read the function computing this, likely near the "Simple, honest heuristic" comment referencing per-mod resource profiling).

## What the owner wants
1. **Better visual design** — this is currently a plain text-in-a-box panel; make it a proper card matching the rest of the page's visual quality (the mod card redesign, hero fixes, etc. from tonight — check `components/mods/` for the established visual language: real box-art/icon treatment, proper button styling via existing `btn-primary`/`btn-secondary` classes, spacing conventions).
2. **A real button that deploys the actual game's server** — not a plain text link. It should link to wherever `/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`'s new deploy-section (`PlanConfigurator`, built earlier tonight in `components/marketing/gamelanding/PlanConfigurator.tsx` and `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`'s `PREVIEW_GAMES`) actually sends someone to deploy — reuse the REAL href/flow that page already uses, don't invent a second path. If `PREVIEW_GAMES[family]` doesn't exist for this family (confirmed earlier tonight this is true for `schedule1`, which has no real Nxeon hosting plan), the button must not appear/must honestly reflect that — check for this case explicitly, don't show a broken deploy button for games we don't actually host.
3. **If the signed-in customer ALREADY has a server for this game family**: instead of (or in addition to) a "deploy new server" button, show:
   - An "Open [server name]" button/link per existing server, going to that server's real management page (check how `QuickAddButton.tsx`/`app/dashboard/nxlabs/page.tsx` already resolve "servers eligible for this family" — likely `serversByFamily` from `familyFor()` in `lib/game-config.ts`, already used elsewhere on the mod pages).
   - A "Deploy another server" option alongside (customers can and do run multiple servers for the same game).
   - **For EACH existing eligible server**, a real "Add this mod to [server name]" action — this should call the SAME real install path already used elsewhere (`QuickAddButton.tsx` calls `installMod()` — check `lib/actions-mods.ts` or wherever that server action lives) rather than inventing a new install mechanism. If there's already a `QuickAddButton` component that does exactly this for a LIST of servers, this may be mostly a matter of placing/styling it correctly in this specific panel rather than building new install logic — read `QuickAddButton.tsx` in full first, this is very likely already 90% built for the mod-card use case and just needs to be composed into this panel too.
   - This is PORTAL-ONLY logic (a public/marketing visitor has no servers) — confirm how the codebase already distinguishes "am I logged in with real servers" vs. anonymous (the mod card's `footer` prop is only passed by `serversByFamily`-aware portal callers per the comment in `StoreBrowser.tsx` around line 195-197 — follow that same convention here) and make sure the marketing-side page shows the plain "deploy a server" CTA (no server list, since there isn't a logged-in customer to have one) while the portal-side page shows the full existing-server/add-to-server treatment.

## CRITICAL process rule (still in force)
Multiple agents running their own `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` concurrently corrupted the build output earlier tonight and caused a real production outage. **Do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, poll every 30s until clear. Make your changes, verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`, commit and push to `main`, then STOP. I (the parent session) am batching commits and will deploy everything together myself.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read both mod detail page files, `lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s recommended-plan logic, `components/mods/QuickAddButton.tsx`, `components/marketing/gamelanding/PlanConfigurator.tsx`, and `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` in full before editing.
- DB reads only via `db` from `lib/db` if needed. Never print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Commit and push to `main` (check `git log origin/main` before/after for concurrent pushes — there is other active work landing in this same tree tonight, coordinate/re-pull rather than force-push).

Report back: what the redesigned card looks like, confirmation the deploy button reuses the real existing pricing/deploy flow (not a second invented one), confirmation the existing-server/add-to-server case reuses the real existing install action, how you handled the schedule1 no-hosting-plan edge case, and confirmation you committed without deploying.
